{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 with recent negative spikes) to avoid overestimating price stability.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, as models tend to overreact to recent price drops.",
    "When sentiment shifts from neutral to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 or 0.50), increase forecast mean slightly to reflect potential upward momentum, but avoid sharp spikes.",
    "If model forecasts show a sharp upward spike followed by a correction, reduce the peak value by 5-10% to account for overshoot bias.",
    "In periods with sustained high sentiment (e.g., 0.50+), apply a mild upward bias to forecast mean, but cap at 10% above recent high to prevent overcorrection.",
    "When true outcomes show strong mean reversion (e.g., prices falling after a spike), adjust forecasts to align with recent 5-10 day average, especially if sentiment is neutral.",
    "For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day), reduce forecast variance if sentiment is stable or mildly negative, as models tend to overestimate volatility in flat periods."
  ]
}
